rounds.text: Omax Autos Ltd trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 8.82x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 5.93x [E6], offering compelling value compared to broader sector benchmarks. The business is demonstrating explosive operational acceleration, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 48% [E17], quarterly sales soaring by 88% YoY [E66], and an eye-catching 316% surge in compounded profit growth over the same TTM period [E21]. Furthermore, profitability is firmly backed by strong cash generation, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 67 Cr and free cash flow at Rs 66 Cr for March 2026, alongside an exceptional cash conversion ratio of 1.81x [E34, E35, E36]. The company is also conservatively financed with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.12x [E37] and has actively reduced its borrowings down to Rs 42 Cr [E39]. Conceded: long-term historical sales growth has been negative at -7% over 10 years [E14], and the company carries a low 3-year average return on equity of 2.81% [E63]. Nonetheless, rules-based screening backs this momentum with a solid score of 87 out of 100 [E65], supported by an increasing yearly operating margin trend spanning the last 7 years [E32] and a healthy dividend yield of 2.34% [E4].

Conceded: [E45], which points to a higher discounted cash flow intrinsic value. However, the business carries structural weaknesses and risks that the bullish narrative ignores, starting with a historical top-line contraction showing a compounded sales growth over 10 years of -7% [E14]. Furthermore, long-term profitability metrics are exceptionally depressed, evidenced by a median return on equity over 10 years of -3% and a 5-year median ROE of -2% [E26, E27]. The recent earnings quality is also compromised, because reported earnings include a non-operating component of Rs. 34.3 Cr in other income [E64]. Institutional confidence is actively withdrawing from the counter, demonstrated by a negative institutional money flow reading and a holding decrease of 0.43 percentage points [E44, E70]. Finally, shareholders face extreme historical volatility of 56.6% paired with a severe worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -90.8% [E53, E54].

Conceded: [E14] and [E26], which document long-term historical top-line contraction of -7% and a 10-year median ROE of -3%. However, the bear's emphasis on past struggles ignores an extraordinary operational turnaround, evidenced by a 5-year sales growth rate of 25% and a massive trailing twelve-month expansion of 48% [E15, E17]. Conceded: [E64] regarding the inclusion of other income in earnings. Yet profit growth has surged dramatically, with a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 316% and a 3-year profit growth of 49% [E20, E21], supported by robust operating margin expansion to 11% and solid cash generation yielding Rs 66 Cr in free cash flow [E30, E36]. Conceded: [E44] and [E70], confirming negative institutional money flow. This institutional exit, however, fails to negate the stellar relative-strength score of 100 and a 71.6% twelve-month price return that demonstrate strong momentum [E51, E52]. Conceded: [E53] and [E54], highlighting historical volatility and a severe past drawdown. Nevertheless, the company is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.12x and a healthy dividend yield of 2.34% [E4, E37], shielding current investors from the structural risks of the past.

Conceded: [E15], [E17], [E20], [E21], [E30], [E36], [E51], [E52], [E57], [E61], and [E66] regarding recent revenue expansion, profit surges, margin improvements, cash generation, and momentum metrics. However, the bull's framing of an operational turnaround glosses over structural weaknesses, notably a 10-year compounded sales growth of -7% and a multi-year median return on equity that remains deeply depressed at -3% over ten years and -2% over five years [E14, E26, E27]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes the institutional exit [E44, E70] and the presence of non-operating items, specifically noting that earnings include Rs 34.3 Cr of other income which distorts the true quality of operational performance [E64]. The bull's dismissal of historical volatility also fails to account for a record peak-to-trough drawdown of -90.8% and an annualized volatility of 56.6% [E53, E54]. Finally, while the debt-to-equity ratio is currently low at 0.12x [E37], historical balance sheet strain is evidenced by a concerning current ratio of 0.87x where current liabilities exceeded current assets [E38].
